implementation_notes: In the actor ecosystem Pekko - Akka's Apache-licensed successor - ships the channel as EventStream: a pub-sub stream of events whose subscribers are ActorRefs and whose channels are classes, so publishing an event delivers it to every subscriber registered for that class or a supertype (SubchannelClassification). That replaces a hand-written observer registry with subscribe/unsubscribe/publish on the actor system. Outside the actor libraries the pattern is a hand-written listener list, and for stream-shaped fan-out with back-pressure Akka Streams' BroadcastHub gives each subscriber its own stream.
code_sketch:
val system = ActorSystem("shop")
val billing: ActorRef = system.actorOf(Props[BillingListener]())
system.eventStream.subscribe(billing, classOf[OrderPlaced])   // class = topic
system.eventStream.publish(OrderPlaced("o-1"))                // every subscriber receives it
system.eventStream.unsubscribe(billing)
pitfalls: Subscribing to a class also subscribes to its subtypes: a listener for a broad base type receives more events than intended.
ActorRef subscribers have bounded mailboxes: a slow subscriber's overflow behaviour is the mailbox policy's, not the event stream's, so a growing mailbox is the failure mode to watch.
EventStream is scoped to one ActorSystem; components wired to different ActorSystems silently stop seeing each other's events.
